title: Each Plan of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans Answers Only for the Piece Named on It
content:
Where a customer holds several plans of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans, each plan answers only for the piece named on it and allowances are never pooled across plans. A claim is settled against the allowance of the plan covering the piece claimed for, and where that allowance is short the shortfall is not taken from another plan the customer holds. Where the remaining allowance reaches zero the plan is recorded as exhausted and further claims on it are refused on the ground that the allowance is consumed.

## Points of judgement

- The plan that answers is the one covering the piece claimed for. Two pieces that sound alike over the telephone may sit on different plans entirely, and the covered item reference on the plan record, not the description the customer gives, decides which plan is in question.
- A shortfall on one plan is a shortfall. It is never met from a second plan the same customer holds, however much allowance that second plan has standing.
- Exhaustion is a standing of the plan: once the allowance is consumed the plan is recorded as exhausted, and a claim brought afterwards is refused on the ground that the allowance is consumed.

## Clause no longer in force

The following clause of this basis note is **no longer in force** and is superseded by the current basis; it is kept here only so that the withdrawn law is not applied:

> The benefit consumed in the current coverage year on one plan is read as the sum of the settlements booked to that plan in that year, and the remaining allowance is the granted allowance less that sum.

The yearly and lifetime benefit allowances the plans set, and whether the yearly allowance is granted afresh, remain as the schedules for the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans publish them.
